# Overview

For \~30 gastruloid papers, citation graphs alone poorly separate **experimental protocol** from **biological findings**. Free browsers (@tbl-nocode-tools) help exploration; a **section-aware dual-view** pipeline (@fig-pipeline) is better for a review-quality taxonomy [@singh2023scirepeval; @specter2].

Represent each paper with two views (protocol vs insight), not one fused embedding early on:

$$\mathbf{z}_i^{\mathrm{prot}},\;
\mathbf{z}_i^{\mathrm{ins}}
\in \mathbb{R}^{d}$$ {#eq-dual-views}

Similarity is cosine on each view separately:

$$S_{ij}^{(v)}
=
\frac{
\langle \mathbf{z}_i^{(v)}, \mathbf{z}_j^{(v)} \rangle
}{
\|\mathbf{z}_i^{(v)}\|_2\,\|\mathbf{z}_j^{(v)}\|_2
}
,\qquad
v \in \{\mathrm{prot},\mathrm{ins}\}$$ {#eq-cosine}

```{mermaid}

  Q -->|Yes| Full[Full open pipeline]
  Full --> A[a. GROBID PDF → TEI sections]
  A --> B[b. Feature engineering:<br/>Methods = protocol<br/>Results/Discussion = insights]
  B --> C[c. scispaCy / PubTator3<br/>→ MeSH + GO]
  C --> D[d. Free scientific embeddings<br/>SciBERT / SPECTER2]
  D --> E[e. Cosine similarity matrices]
  E --> F[f. Hierarchical / modular clustering<br/>HDBSCAN or Leiden]
  F --> H[h. BERTopic cluster labels]
  H --> I[i. NetworkX or Neo4j graphs]
  I --> J[j. Intrinsic validation<br/>silhouette / DB / CH]
  Explore --> Out([Literature map])
  J --> Out
```

## No-code path

| Tool | Free | Signal | Role here |
|------------------|------------------|------------------|------------------|
| Citrus Search [@citrussearch] | ✓ | Content embeddings | Best no-code match for protocol/content grouping |
| Inciteful [@inciteful] | ✓ | Citations + similarity | Landmark neighbourhoods; missing papers |
| Connected Papers [@connectedpapers] | Limited | Citation graph | Visual splits (species, tissue, signalling) |

: Free no-code tools for a small gastruloid corpus

Prefer **Citrus** for content/protocol likeness and **Inciteful** for citation neighbourhoods; treat Connected Papers as an optional visual check [@citrussearch; @inciteful; @connectedpapers].

## Full pipeline (summarised)

### a. Paper extraction — GROBID

Parse PDFs to scholarly TEI/XML (title, abstract, sections, references) [@grobid]. Normalise headings to `methods`, `results`, `discussion`, `captions`; exclude the reference list from clustering features.

### b. Feature engineering — protocol vs insights

Do **not** fuse views yet. Build:

- **Protocol text** — methods (+ captions / supplementary methods when present)
- **Insight text** — results + discussion (+ abstract/conclusion)

Optionally fill a short schema (species, aggregate size, CHIR/RA timing, assays, main phenotype) to support later filtering; classic gastruloid axes include mESC aggregates and WNT/CHIR timing [@vandenbrink2014].

### c. Ontology matching — scispaCy

Run biomedical NER (scispaCy; optionally PubTator3) and map entities to **MeSH** / **GO** [@scispacy; @pubtator3; @mesh; @geneontology]. Store as sparse flags or TF–IDF over ontology IDs to stabilise synonym variants (e.g. CHIR / CHIR99021).

### d. Embeddings — free scientific models

Use non-commercial scientific encoders: **SPECTER2** (title+abstract paper anchor) and/or **SciBERT** (section/chunk encoding) [@specter2; @beltagy2019scibert; @singh2023scirepeval]. Pool chunk embeddings into $\mathbf{z}^{\mathrm{prot}}$ and $\mathbf{z}^{\mathrm{ins}}$ (@eq-dual-views); L2-normalise for cosine (@eq-cosine).

### e. Similarity matrices

Compute exact cosine matrices $S^{(\mathrm{prot})}$ and $S^{(\mathrm{ins})}$ (@eq-cosine). With \~30 papers, ANN indices are unnecessary.

### f. Clustering — hierarchical or modular

Prefer **hierarchical** structure or **module-based** partitions:

- agglomerative clustering (average linkage on cosine) + dendrogram; or
- **HDBSCAN** for hierarchical density clusters with outliers [@mcinnes2017hdbscan]; or
- **Leiden** on a $k$-NN similarity graph for modular communities [@traag2019leiden].

Run protocol and insight spaces **separately**, then cross-tabulate cluster memberships (@tbl-outputs).

### h. Cluster labelling — BERTopic

Label clusters with BERTopic / c-TF-IDF terms grounded in member sections [@grootendorst2022bertopic], e.g. `mouse mESC · CHIR-pulse · axial organisation`.

### i. Visualisation — NetworkX or Neo4j

Export papers as nodes and high-similarity edges as a graph in NetworkX (local) or Neo4j (queryable) [@networkx; @neo4j]. Optionally project embeddings with UMAP for a 2D map [@mcinnes2018umap] — plots support interpretation, they are not the clustering itself.

### j. Mathematical validation

Report intrinsic metrics (silhouette, Davies–Bouldin, Calinski–Harabasz) on each view [@rousseeuw1987silhouette]. With a small expert-labelled pair set, add ARI/NMI and Precision\@k for nearest neighbours. Case-check that known families (mouse/CHIR/axial; human RA/Matrigel posterior; tissue-specialised outputs) reappear [@vandenbrink2014].

| Output | Content |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| Protocol clusters | Families of induction / culture / perturbation pipelines |
| Insight clusters | Families of biological claims and phenotypes |
| Protocol × insight cross-tab | Same method, different claims (or the reverse) |

: Linked outputs from the dual-view clustering design

# Python modules (pipeline roles)

| Module / tool | Role in the pipeline |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| `grobid` (service) | PDF → structured TEI sections [@grobid] |
| `scispacy` | Biomedical NER / sentence processing [@scispacy] |
| PubTator3 API | Concept annotation & relations [@pubtator3] |
| `transformers` + SciBERT / SPECTER2 | Free scientific embeddings [@beltagy2019scibert; @specter2] |
| `sentence-transformers` | Convenient pooling / cosine helpers [@reimers2019sbert] |
| `numpy` / `scipy` | Similarity matrices (@eq-cosine) |
| `hdbscan` | Hierarchical density clustering [@mcinnes2017hdbscan] |
| `leidenalg` / `igraph` | Modular graph clustering [@traag2019leiden] |
| `bertopic` | Cluster topic labels [@grootendorst2022bertopic] |
| `networkx` | Local similarity graphs [@networkx] |
| `neo4j` (optional) | Persist/query paper networks [@neo4j] |
| `umap-learn` | 2D visualisation of embeddings [@mcinnes2018umap] |
| `scikit-learn` | Agglomerative clustering; silhouette & related metrics [@rousseeuw1987silhouette] |

: Python and related tooling mentioned in the full pipeline

# Recommendation

Start with @tbl-nocode-tools if the goal is orientation. For a publication-quality gastruloid map, follow @fig-pipeline (full branch): GROBID → dual protocol/insight features → ontology terms → SciBERT/SPECTER2 → cosine $S$ → hierarchical/modular clustering → BERTopic labels → NetworkX/Neo4j → intrinsic validation (@eq-dual-views; @eq-cosine; @tbl-outputs; @tbl-python-modules).
